title: Catalogue of Exploitable Judge Biases: A Red-Team Taxonomy

original_idea.body:
# Catalogue of Exploitable Judge Biases: A Red-Team Taxonomy

**Problem:** There is no compact empirically-ranked catalogue of which small-model-judge biases are most exploitable by a debater.

**Direction:** Enumerate candidate judge biases (length, authority, jargon, formatting, hedging, order, sentiment). For each, craft a minimal manipulative argument exploiting only that bias and measure the shift toward a wrong answer. Rank biases by exploitability and check persistence across judges.

**Why it matters:** Produces a prioritized reusable threat list for anyone hardening oversight.

**Relevant context:** AISI Alignment Project; arXiv:2409.15268; Kenton et al. (2024).

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: a ranked exploitable-bias catalogue is reusable threat infrastructure addressing a named open problem.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Crafting per-bias manipulative arguments + measuring shifts is guided, inference-only.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused per-bias exploitability ranking; enumerating many biases adds breadth.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Red-team threat-mapping on public judges labs deprioritize; external-friendly.

novelty.reasoning: Individual judge biases documented; a unified exploitability ranking may be partly open.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Individual biases known; ranked exploitability catalogue plausibly open.
